knowledge_candidates.text: mxschmitt/action-tmate v3.24 (released 2026-05-29) has no max-duration input and no continue parameter: action.yml declares only sudo, install-dependencies, limit-access-to-actor, detached, connect-timeout-seconds, tmate-server-*, msys2-location, github-token. The session lifetime is bounded by the step/job timeout-minutes, and 'continuing the workflow' means creating the FILE /continue or $GITHUB_WORKSPACE/continue (src/index.js:268-271). Any design that wants a 'max-duration' must write timeout-minutes instead; passing max-duration only produces an 'Unexpected input' warning and does nothing.

limit-access-to-actor defaults to 'auto', which is NOT safe by default: with no public SSH key on the dispatcher's GitHub profile the action logs a warning and starts a session anyone can join. Only the literal true forces users.listPublicKeysForUser(actor) and throws 'No public SSH keys registered with <login>' when that list is empty. For a public repository the run log (and therefore the connection string) is world readable, so 'auto' plus no registered key is a fully open shell. The Web shell URL, when printed, is a bearer link and is not covered by the key check.

Standard GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest runners have no usable /dev/kvm (nested virtualisation is a Linux larger-runner feature), and this pipeline does not need it: scripts/ci/qemu-smoke.sh hardcodes -accel tcg. Measured 2026-11-10 from run 42815980945: a uefi-disk boot takes 55-61 s, the s4 job 5 min 01 s, and the s4 section from checkout to a finished disk image 62 s. s5 boot 3 ('commit the upgraded slot and reclaim') consumed its entire 900 s CI_QEMU_TIMEOUT and failed, so any manual or CI boot of the post-upgrade slot needs a budget above 900 s.

A manual debugging workflow reuses scripts/ci/ through their documented local interface instead of duplicating stage logic: CI_OUTPUT_ENV writes a KEY=VALUE file per stage, ci_load_env_file exports it as CI_*, and the resolved values that must survive into later steps are copied into $GITHUB_ENV with the same lowercase->CI_ mapping. That keeps ci-debug.yml unable to drift from ci-s4/ci-s5, and it is why tests/modules/ci/test_step_env.sh now distinguishes 'wired by env:' from 'wired by the loader' while forbidding the loader in every stage workflow.

Adding any file to .github/workflows changes the CI cache key: scripts/ci/resolve.sh hashes every .github/workflows/*.yml into it, so the first run after landing a new workflow re-downloads rootfs/kernel/kmods from the mirror and only then settles. Expect one slower run, not a regression. Also, a new ci-*.yml file is picked up by tests/modules/ci/test_pipeline.sh's stage glob and by tests/modules/ci/test_step_env.sh's static env wiring scan, so a non-stage workflow with that name prefix needs both tests told what it is.
